messages:
jamie.ops: Heads up — we rolled NCCL 2.18.5 to the us-west-2 GPU pool at 07:30 and are seeing intermittent hangs on multi-GPU inference jobs (mainly 4+ GPU shards).

marta.ml: Details? hangs during init or collectives? any error logs?

jamie.ops: Hangs appear during the warmup allreduce stage, jobs just sit at 0.0 tokens/sec. No OOMs. Docker logs show blocked on ncclCommInitRank in some workers.

ryan.runtime: Possible P2P/kernel mismatch. What drivers/CUDA are those nodes on?

jamie.ops: Driver 535.86, CUDA 12.1, some nodes are running slightly older kernels (5.15) because of delayed kernel patching. Hardware: A100 80GB on the affected pool.

diego.sre: We saw similar on a different cluster when NCCL used IB/GDR paths. Can you paste NCCL debug output? Try NCCL_DEBUG=INFO before killing the process.

jamie.ops: Pasted snippet from one hung worker:```
NCCL INFO NET/IB : Using device mlx5_0 for ndev 0, pci 0000:03:00.0
NCCL WARN Call to socket failed errno=110 (Connection timed out)
NCCL WARN Unhandled error, aborting.
# stack: [0x7f6a3c...], ncclCommInitRank+0x1d2
```

marta.ml: That looks like IB timeouts. Can you try disabling IB for a test job? envs: NCCL_IB_DISABLE=1 NCCL_P2P_DISABLE=1

jamie.ops: Started a repro with NCCL_IB_DISABLE=1 — job progressed past the hang point, throughput is lower (~1.8x slower) but stable.

ryan.runtime: So regression tied to IB/GDR path in 2.18.5. Any kernel logs (dmesg) showing mlx5 resets?

jamie.ops: dmesg shows a few mlx5_core timeouts on two hosts, then the driver recovers. snippet:```
mlx5_core 0000:03:00.0 enp3s0f0: firmware error, resetting
mlx5_core 0000:03:00.0: Reset adapter due to fatal error
```

diego.sre: OK this smells like an interaction between NCCL 2.18.5 IB codepath and our mlx5 firmware/driver. Quick mitigation: set NCCL_IB_DISABLE=1 in the rollout for us-west-2 and WT rollback the NCCL bump for Dedicated.

jamie.ops: Agreed. We're toggling NCCL_IB_DISABLE for the running inference daemonset and starting a staggered rollback of the image tag to 2.17.3 on non-critical pools. Will coordinate with deploy-bot.

deploy-bot: @jamie.ops started rollout:redwood-inference-runtime/worker -> image:nccl-2.17.3 (15 nodes at a time).

marta.ml: Long-term: we should reproduce in a lab with same kernel/driver/firmware and open with Mellanox/NVIDIA. Also validate whether 2.18.6 or a driver bump fixes this.

ryan.runtime: Agreed. Add a canary job with NCCL 2.18.6 + driver 536.x in staging and run multi-GPU inference harness with NCCL_DEBUG=INFO,NCCL_DEBUG_SUBSYS=ALL. Also test with NCCL_P2P_DISABLE=0/1, GDR toggles.

jamie.ops: Created canary tickets and scheduled a weekend test window. Ticket: INFRA-1723. Notes attached with repro command:
```bash
export NCCL_DEBUG=INFO NCCL_IB_DISABLE=0 NCCL_P2P_DISABLE=0
docker run --gpus all redwood/inference:canary sh -c "python -m infra.multi_gpu_repro --gpus 4 --batch 1 --profile"
```

diego.sre: For customers worried about latency hit from disabling IB, we can route golden traffic to dedicated nodes that remain on old NCCL while we rollout the fix.

jamie.ops: Doing that now. Also marking affected customer tickets and flagging us-west-2 in the console as degraded for multi-GPU collectives.

marta.ml: If anyone hits other oddities (timeouts, collectives stalling but processes still alive) drop logs here. We'll escalate to NVIDIA if we can reproduce in lab. :+1:

infra-bot: Incident created: INC-2026-08-NCCL-HANGS assigned to jamie.ops, severity: medium.

jamie.ops: Follow-ups: 1) rollback or disable IB in prod (in progress), 2) canary 2.18.6 + 536 driver in staging, 3) firmware/drivers inventory + open vendor ticket.

ryan.runtime: Also add a perf benchmark before/after to quantify the cost of the temporary IB disable. Put results in the ticket.

jamie.ops: Will update INFRA-1723 with numbers. Thanks team.
